html:
The Ganden Phodrang was the government of Tibet led by the Dalai Lamas, from 1642 to 1959. It was named after the residence of the Dalai Lamas at Drepung Monastery.

It began when the Mongol lord Güshi Khan defeated the king of Tsang and, in a ceremony at Shigatse, gave power over Tibet to the 5th Dalai Lama. Lhasa became the capital again. Religious and political power were joined in one office, held by a reincarnate lama, with regents ruling while he was a child.

From 1720 the Tibetan government came under the protection of the Qing, who kept officials in Lhasa, though real control varied a great deal. After the Qing fell in 1912, Tibet ran its own affairs. The Chinese army entered in 1950, and after the failed uprising of 1959 the 14th Dalai Lama fled to India. The government lives on in exile as the Central Tibetan Administration.
sum: The Ganden Phodrang was the government of Tibet led by the Dalai Lamas, from 1642 to 1959. It was named after the residence of the Dalai Lamas at Drepung Monastery.
